parts.markdown:
Our free **Arizona paycheck calculator** helps you estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Arizona income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly earnings, select your payment frequency and enter your Arizona withholding amount to calculate your estimated net paycheck.

Arizona's individual income tax rate is relatively straightforward, but employees can select different payroll withholding percentages. Understanding the relationship between your selected percentage and actual tax liability can help you manage your earnings more effectively.

Whether you work in Phoenix, Tucson, Scottsdale, Mesa or another Arizona community, this calculator can help you compare salaries and prepare your budget.

## How to Use the Arizona Paycheck Calculator

Select annual salary or hourly wages, depending on your employment arrangement.

Enter your gross income before taxes and choose your payment frequency.

Enter federal and Arizona income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub, including any extra withholding.

Add retirement contributions, health insurance premiums and other applicable employee deductions.

Review the paycheck breakdown to understand how much is deducted for federal taxes, Arizona withholding and payroll contributions.

If you are uncertain about your withholding percentage, check your most recent pay stub or ask your employer's payroll department.

Arizona generally does not impose a separate employee-funded unemployment insurance deduction under ordinary employment arrangements.

Local governments may collect other taxes, but these should not automatically be included as personal income tax deductions.

## How Arizona State Income Tax Works

Arizona applies a flat individual income tax rate of 2.5%.

However, the state income tax calculated on your annual return is not necessarily the same percentage your employer deducts from every paycheck.

Your annual taxable income may differ from your gross earnings because of deductions and other adjustments.

Arizona payroll withholding instead uses a percentage elected by the employee and applied to gross taxable wages.

For example, an employee might elect 2% withholding even though the statutory individual income tax rate is 2.5%.

Whether this election produces sufficient withholding depends on the employee's overall income, deductions, credits and other circumstances.

The [Arizona Department of Revenue withholding guidance](https://azdor.gov/individuals/withholding-tax-individual) explains how employees can select or change their withholding arrangements.

## Understanding Arizona Form A-4

Form A-4 allows employees to specify the percentage of gross taxable earnings their employer should withhold for Arizona income tax.

Employees can also request an additional fixed amount to be withheld from each paycheck.

The available percentage elections provide flexibility when managing expected annual tax obligations.

Arizona withholding is separate from your federal Form W-4 elections. Changing federal withholding does not necessarily change your Arizona withholding percentage.

You can obtain the current [Arizona Withholding Percentage Election form](https://azdor.gov/forms/withholding-forms/arizona-withholding-percentage-election) from the Arizona Department of Revenue.

Employees who qualify for zero withholding must meet the applicable requirements rather than simply choosing zero to increase their immediate take-home pay.

## How to Estimate an Appropriate Arizona Withholding Amount

Suppose you estimate that your annual Arizona income tax liability will be $1,500.

Your employer has already withheld $500, leaving an estimated $1,000 to cover.

If you expect another 20 paychecks during the year, your remaining withholding target would be:

$1,000 ÷ 20 = $50 per paycheck

If each paycheck contains $2,000 in Arizona taxable wages, a 2.5% election would produce $50 in withholding.

This example demonstrates how employees can evaluate their withholding needs using estimated annual liability and remaining pay periods.

The [Arizona withholding calculation guide](https://azdor.gov/individuals/withholding-calculations) provides additional instructions for assessing your election.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Arizona Paychecks

### Federal income tax

Federal income tax withholding depends on your taxable wages, filing status, pay frequency and Form W-4 information.

It may also account for multiple jobs, eligible credits, other income and requested additional withholding.

Employers generally calculate withholding using the methods described in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

### Social Security

Employees generally contribute 6.2% of covered Social Security wages.

For 2026, the annual taxable wage limit is $184,500.

An employee receiving $2,500 in covered wages who has not reached the annual ceiling would contribute $155.

### Medicare

Ordinary Medicare withholding is 1.45% of covered earnings, without a standard annual wage ceiling.

Employers generally collect an additional 0.9% on covered Medicare earnings exceeding $200,000 paid by that employer during the calendar year.

The final tax liability can depend on household income and filing status.

Consult the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) for further information.

## Arizona Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can estimate earnings by multiplying their wage by regular hours and adding any qualifying overtime compensation.

Consider an employee earning $26 per hour who works 40 regular hours and six overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$26 × 40 = $1,040

Overtime earnings:

$26 × 1.5 × 6 = $234

Total gross earnings:

$1,274

If the full amount is subject to Arizona withholding and the employee elects 2%, state withholding would be $25.48.

Federal taxes and other applicable contributions would also be deducted.

Overtime eligibility depends on employment classification and applicable labor rules. Review the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for details.

## Does Arizona Have Local Income Taxes?

Arizona cities generally do not impose separate municipal personal wage income taxes.

Employees in Phoenix, Tucson and other Arizona cities therefore generally do not encounter additional city wage income taxes of the kind imposed by certain municipalities in other states.

However, local sales taxes, housing costs and transportation expenses can influence how much money remains available after payday.

When comparing employment opportunities, consider these living expenses separately from paycheck deductions.

## How Employee Benefits Affect Arizona Take-Home Pay

Retirement contributions, healthcare premiums and other benefits can affect the amount deposited into your bank account.

Traditional 401(k) contributions generally reduce current federal income-taxable wages, while Roth contributions generally do not provide the same immediate income tax reduction.

Qualifying pre-tax health benefits may reduce certain taxable wage amounts.

These deductions can also affect the wage amount used to calculate Arizona withholding.

For example, if eligible deductions reduce Arizona gross taxable wages from $2,500 to $2,300, a 2.5% withholding election would produce a state deduction of $57.50 rather than $62.50.

Always confirm whether each deduction receives the intended tax treatment.

## Comparing Employment Offers in Arizona

A higher salary can provide greater take-home income, but it is important to evaluate your complete compensation package.

Compare employer retirement matching, healthcare premiums, bonuses, paid leave and commuting expenses.

An employee relocating to metropolitan Phoenix may encounter different housing costs from someone working in Tucson or a smaller Arizona community.

Use the calculator to estimate both salaries and determine which opportunity leaves more money available after essential expenses.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is Arizona paycheck withholding always 2.5%?

No. Arizona's individual income tax rate is 2.5%, but employees can elect different paycheck withholding percentages through Form A-4.

### Can I choose zero Arizona income tax withholding?

Only employees who meet the applicable exemption requirements, including expecting no Arizona income tax liability for the year, should elect zero withholding.

### Why do I still owe Arizona income tax after my employer withheld taxes?

Your total withholding may be lower than your final annual liability because of other income, insufficient withholding elections or changes in your circumstances. Review your withholding information and expected tax liability periodically.
